text:
alex: FYI I ran a RoPE-scaling sweep overnight across qwen-7b and mixtral-8x7b. Linear/NTK/YARN variants. Saw a sharp perplexity cliff for the NTK variant on mixtral at long context (>=24k).

maya: can you paste the perf numbers?

alex: brief: qwen-7b stable across all variants up to 32k. mixtral-8x7b: linear & YARN okay; NTK shows +7-12% perplexity at 24k and +25% at 32k vs baseline. latency wise NTK kernel picks a different matmul path causing KV cache churn.

ryan: interesting — did kernel selector flip to fallback kernels for NTK?

alex: yes. profiler shows kernel_selector choosing smaller GEMM kernels when head_dim % 64 != 0 (mixtral has odd head dims after NTK scaling). excerpt from runlog: 

```
[2026-03-17 03:12:08] kernel_selector: model=mixtral-8x7b variant=ntk scale=1.15 -> selected_kernel=gemm_small_avx, fallback_latency=14.2ms
[2026-03-17 03:12:08] kv_cache: hit_rate=0.78, cache_compact_ops=3
[2026-03-17 03:12:08] batching: avg_batch=8, continuous_batching=true, prefix_cache_applied=true
```

maya: hmm cache_compact_ops spikes could indicate KV layout fragmentation after NTK remap. Did you run a KV-only microbench?

alex: ran kv microbench: NTK mixtral shows +18% per-token KV lookup time when sequence > 16k. command: `./bench_kv --model mixtral-8x7b-ntk --seq 32768 --threads 4`. output snippet:

```
KV_LOOKUP_MS: 0.42 0.44 0.43 0.50 0.61 0.69 0.85 0.98
(steep increase after 16384)
```

sophia: is the matrix layout different because NTK scaling changed rotary frequencies -> misaligned block packing?

ryan: likely. We pack heads into nvcc-friendly blocks of 64. If head_dim changes post-scaling to non-multiples, we pad and end up with extra memcpy and slower kernels.

alex: kernel selection logs confirm pad path. Also saw increased memcpy ratio in profiler: memcpy_cpu_to_gpu jumped from 2% -> 9% of step time for those configs.

perf-bot: Benchmark artifact: https://internal.perf/reports/1852509876 (uploaded) :white_check_mark:

maya: do we have a quick patch? two ideas: force kernel selector to use large_gemm with padded tensors (may increase compute but saves memcpy) OR update batching heuristic to favour smaller micro-batches to avoid huge KV pages.

ryan: forcing large kernel might hurt latency at low concurrency. Another option: a runtime rewrite to keep KV contiguous layout by using head-wise packing at allocate time, not on first write. That removes fragmentation.

alex: I prototyped forcing contiguous KV allocation -> eliminated the memcpy spike and restored perplexity to within 3% of baseline. Patch included in gist: https://internal.gists/ropexp/contig-kv-alloc

sophia: can you paste the config snippet you used?

alex: sure:

```yaml
# runtime tuning snippet
model: mixtral-8x7b-ntk
rope_variant: ntk
kv_allocation: contiguous_force: true
kernel_selector: prefer_large_gemm_if_padding_over=0.1  # fraction of padded elements
batching:
  max_batch_tokens: 4096
  prefer_latency: true
  continuous_batching: true
```

maya: nice. Did you test for side effects on qwen? Qwen tends to have different head/kvdims.

alex: yes — contiguous alloc is safe; it slightly increases memory footprint (~3%) for qwen but no perf regression. For mixtral-ntk it improves latency by ~10% at 24k.

ryan: what's the implication for kernel selection heuristics? Should we change the rule that picks small kernels based solely on head_dim remainder? Maybe add a cost model including memcpy overhead and kv_cache_hit_rate.

alex: exactly. I propose updating kernel selector to evaluate estimated memcpy + packing cost: cost = compute_est + memcpy_est - kv_cache_hit_bonus. If cost_large < cost_small choose large.

sophia: and for batching heuristics? We saw continuous_batching + prefix_cache helps qwen but for mixtral-ntk huge continuous prefix leads to giant KV pages; maybe cap continuous prefix length per-model-variant.

maya: propose safe ranges table (per-model-variant) and automatic rollback. Example: mixtral-8x7b-ntk safe_seq <= 20k; mixtral-8x7b-linear safe_seq <= 32k; qwen-7b-ntk safe_seq <= 32k. We should store this in model-profile metadata.

alex: agreed. I'll draft PR to add per-variant safe_seq param and hook into router to reject requests beyond safe_seq unless override flag set.

perf-bot: Regression alert: mixtral-8x7b-ntk saw +22% token latency at 32k on canary yesterday. Ticket: INF-4273

maya: add test to perf-suite: longctx_kv_consistency and kernel_choice_cost_model. Also add a microbench that simulates mixed concurrency + long prefixes.

ryan: action items:
- alex: PR for contiguous KV alloc and safe_seq metadata (ETA 1 day)
- maya: add perf-suite tests and automation (ETA 2 days)
- sophia: update kernel selector cost model spec (ETA 3 days)
- ops: hold canary for mixtral-ntk until patch lands

alex: I'll post the PR link once ready. For now we've pinned mixtral-ntk to conservative safe_seq 20k on canary.

sophia: thanks — big win to catch this early.

alex: thanks all :thumbsup:
